name: crustc
tagline: The rustc compiler translated into 46 million lines of C
description: crustc is a C translation of the entire rustc 1.98.0-nightly compiler — roughly 46 million lines of C that builds with GCC and make. The resulting Rust compiler can compile core, alloc, and std, and it is network-transparent, meaning it can even talk to a C compiler over TCP. Built over three years across 14 attempts, crustc's goal is to bring Rust to old or obscure hardware that has no LLVM backend; it has already successfully compiled Rust for Plan 9.
highlights: Entire rustc 1.98.0-nightly translated to ~46 million lines of C
Builds with GCC and make — no LLVM required
Compiles core, alloc, and std; already compiled Rust for Plan 9
Network-transparent: can talk to a C compiler over TCP
Three years of work across 14 attempts
curatorNote: A three-year, 14-attempt effort to translate the entire rustc into C so Rust can run where LLVM cannot. It already compiles for Plan 9. Absurd in the best way — and a genuinely important portability experiment.
